newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- APPLE DAILY - More than half of Hong Kong people believe the laws on right of abode should be legislated by the Legislative Council, only 19.8 percent said it should be done by the provisional legislature, according to the paper's survey.
- ECONOMIC TIMES - Secretary for Housing Dominic Wong held talks with property developers last Friday. He urged them not to participate in property speculation and have self-dicipline.

- SING TAO - Sources said the Preparatory Committee would be disbanded after June 30. But it said some of the members believed the committee should continue to function until the setting up of the first post-handover legislature.

- MAD DOG DAILY - The dipute on the right of abode was because of provisional legislature. Britain wanted the Legislative Council to pass the bill, but China wanted the provisional legislature to legislate.

- ECONOMIC JOURNAL - A source said Tung would not visit the United States before the July 1 handover. He will go to Washington as the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Chief Executive after the sovereignty transfer.

- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - Government officials warned that right-of-abode lawsuits would abound and the immigration system could be paralysed if the provisional legislature passed residency laws before July 1.
- A recent poll showed fewer people than two months ago feel happy about the handover.
- Business leaders expressed alarm at proposed changes to immigration laws that could restrict their travel rights.

- HONG KONG STANDARD - The government has underestimated the number of mainland children born to Hong Kong residents who are waiting to be reunited with their families by about 100,000, according to Guangdong Public Security Buearu figures.

- Peregrine Investments Holdings is to send an international accountancy firm to Bangladesh to audit the figures of its local office to prove its innocence in the events which led to the country's worst stock market crash last year.
